{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Budget is shown, not assumed. Files.com ($199–499/mo) and Nodinite (~$3,600/yr) have published prices for this exact capability. That suggests B2B teams pay for file-arrival monitoring. Idea B's only paid reference is a single $1.99/mo Pro tier, with no evidence anyone buys it.",
    "One B2B customer is easier to win than paying consumers. At $49–199/mo, a single customer validates Idea A. Idea B's $1.99–5/mo price needs free-to-paid conversion, and its own brief calls that rate unknown.",
    "Idea B's competition is free in a way that blocks payment. Four maintained competitors are free, several are open source, and they cover the same Reddit use case. Idea A's paid competitors are mostly full platforms (MFT suites, data platforms), which leaves an opening for a cheaper standalone tool for teams without one. Idea A's main risk, self-built cron scripts, is real but weaker than free, ready-made substitutes.",
    "Idea B carries harm and platform risks Idea A does not. Noisy AI detection that falsely flags real users could hurt the core use case. The extension also depends on third-party page structures and terms of service it does not control.",
    "Both ideas are equally buildable. Each brief rates the core build as low-complexity for an AI-agent-run, six-week build, so build effort does not separate them."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's price anchor, ReviewGuard's $1.99/month Pro tier, is the only evidence of willingness to pay. It shows a listed price, not purchases. It also covers Google Maps/TripAdvisor reviews, not the Reddit spam-filtering use case. The brief admits no competitor publishes install or revenue numbers.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Idea A's demand evidence is thin and dated: two forum quotes from 2012 and 2016, plus an unquoted HN link. Its acquisition channel is uncertain, and the SEO cost estimate is marked [unsourced]. Its own case against, bundling by Files.com and easy self-building, is serious. Idea A wins mainly because Idea B's evidence points even more strongly to zero willingness to pay, not because Idea A is strongly proven."
}
